title: Allah's Mercy Surpasses His Wrath
summary: Believers should never despair of Allah's mercy, which surpasses His wrath.
translation: A person, even if a believer or a servant of God, may commit many sins and feel distant from God's mercy, but should never despair or lose hope, for despair is disbelief, and Allah does not like those who despair of Him because Allah Himself says that indeed His mercy has surpassed His wrath. This means that no matter the actions that may cause His anger, His wrath cannot go beyond His merciful nature—He is more merciful than wrathful. Thus, people should always remain hopeful in Allah, regardless of their sins and situations that distance them from His mercy. If they bow down in repentance, they should ask for forgiveness, acknowledging His vast mercy. As narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, reported in a Hadith, that Allah has one hundred mercies. He has sent one mercy among jinn, humans, animals, and venomous creatures, which is the reason for their compassion and mercy towards each other—even wild beasts show affection towards their offspring due to this. Allah has reserved ninety-nine mercies with which He will show mercy to His obedient servants on the Day of Judgment. This Hadith is recorded in Bukhari and Muslim, and a similar narration by Salman al-Farsi (may Allah be pleased with him) in Sahih Muslim includes that when the Day of Judgment comes, Allah will complete all hundred mercies, combining the one mercy sent to the world with the ninety-nine retained. This demonstrates that the mercy witnessed between creatures in the world is only an expression of this one mercy sent by Allah. The complete state of the ninety-nine mercies is beyond imagination, and on the Day of Judgment, the totality of these mercies, including the one on earth, will be realized. Thus, believers will benefit from this remarkable mercy, and those who obediently follow Him will have their sins forgiven, with Paradise as their abode.
